newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says North Korea looks stable for now.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says North Korea looks stable for now.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was making routine contingency plans for a range of scenarios in North Korea including possible government collapse but saw no signs of political instability there now.

"We do not see signs at the moment of political instability in North Korea," State Department spokesman John Dinger told a regular press briefing. "But this sort of planning ... is very routine. And of course you and the American people would expect us to make contingency plans."

The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the U.S. military had begun planning a huge international relief effort on the assumption that the food-short North's Stalinist government was headed for collapse.

The newspaper said preliminary talks had been held with South Korea and Japan and some "very general" discussions had been held with China, Pyongyang's long-time ally. The talks focused on what to do if large numbers of hungry people began pouring out of North Korea, it said.
A Pentagon spokeswoman said contingency planning for all types of scenarios was nothing new.
